C1.name: read-contract addition
C1.decision: prepare_layer(&mut self, layer: usize) is a REQUIRED trait method — no default body
C1.reason:
Several of the thirteen implementors forward to an inner provider (the survey first named two — Measured

and Perturbed; wiring the method found six). With a defaulted no-op, a forwarding wrapper that forgot it would compile and silently never prepare its inner provider: codec/v1 under the MEM-1 harness would serve a stale scratch. The frozen range check would refuse that loudly, so it could not become wrong attention — but it would surface only when a codec provider is wrapped, at run time, in the one harness that adjudicates C3. A required method makes the compiler name every implementor, so every wrapper forwards it by construction and every plain provider states, in one line, that it has nothing to prepare. This is the repo's 'a checked default, never an assumed one' applied to the trait itself.
C1.cost_accepted: a one-line no-op in each of the seven providers that lend what they hold (row/v1, canonical/v1, window/v1, ExactRetention, HostileRows — also the plugin fixture's provider — RowsOnly, RowsOnlyLatent), and real forwarding in the six wrappers
C1.signature: fn prepare_layer(&mut self, layer: usize) — no Result: a provider's own state is complete by construction (every row it holds it appended), so preparing it cannot fail on input; an out-of-range layer is the same invariant violation rows(layer) already treats as one
C1.call_sites: immediately before every rows(layer) the executor makes: decode/run.rs softmax step and conv-QKV step, attention_ops.rs attention_into_kv (resumed prefill, per position), layer_exec.rs conv-QKV (batch); batched prefill at position 0 reads no rows and makes no call. No library code outside the executor reads provider rows

C1.acceptance_restated: Every continuation-row read in V3 is preceded by preparation of that exact layer, across fresh prefill, resumed prefill, decode and conv-QKV paths, and wrappers cannot silently omit the preparation boundary. Witnessed dynamically for batched prefill, resumed prefill and decode (prepare_layer.rs; the MEM-1 record); the conv-QKV call sites are structurally present, not dynamically witnessed here (no in-crate conv-QKV fixture). Wrappers cannot omit it silently because the method is required (compile-enforced); a wrapper that implements it as a no-op is refused by name at the step (tested). Forwarding bodies in wrappers that refuse at announcement (NoLatent, RefusingState) never run — the lifecycle boundary working, not a gap
C1.survey_correction: the pre-code survey classified KvOnly, RecordingKvState, NoLatent and RefusingState as plain providers; a first mechanical pass gave them no-op bodies, and reviewing the diff showed each lends self.0/self.inner's rows. Corrected to forward before any build. The required method is what made the four visible: each needed an explicit body, so each was read

can_prove: compressed authority is pluggable under the same continuation contract

design_finding_head_dim.found: the freeze requires blocks of 'the model's head_dim (from the plan's layer geometry — never inferred from kv_dim)', but LayerKvGeometry carries only kv_dim = num_kv_heads × head_dim; the plan's op has head_dim and the geometry drops it
design_finding_head_dim.change: LayerKvGeometry gains `head_dim: usize`, filled from op.head_dim (softmax) and op.geometry.head_dim (conv-QKV) in plan_continuation_geometry; every struct literal states it (36 at base, mostly tests: agnostic test literals use head_dim = kv_dim, one head). The type crosses the plugin boundary (prepare(&[LayerKvGeometry])), so larql-plugin/4 → /5 with /4 refused by name
design_finding_head_dim.coordination: peer sessions with open larql-vindex work were told before code; none constructs the type (confirmed)

design_finding_refusal.found: the codec's WHT requires a power-of-two block; head_dims of 80 or 96 exist in real models, and the codec would panic on one — library code must refuse untrusted input, not panic
design_finding_refusal.change: ContinuationError gains GeometryUnsupported { provider, layer, reason }. codec/v1 overrides prepare_continuation (the only announcement both executor entry points use, and it returns Result) to refuse, by name, any layer whose head_dim is not a power of two or does not divide kv_dim, before a row exists; prepare() treats the same as an invariant

representation.decision: per layer, one allocation per retained POSITION holding that position's encoded K then V blocks (Vec<u8>, exact capacity), in a list with a draining front — window/v1's shape with encoded rows instead of adopted f32 rows
representation.reason: the same reasons W1 recorded for window/v1 (exact base/end, physical release of each dropped position witnessable on its own allocation, drain = a pointer memmove, no wrap-around) plus: append-born live bytes are then exactly rows × encoded_row_bytes, which is the frozen residency formula with the row list as the declared fixed capacity. A per-layer contiguous byte buffer would make every drain a memmove of the whole window's codes (~0.5 MB per sliding layer per token on gemma) and is not smaller
representation.encoded_row_bytes: 2 × (kv_dim / head_dim) × (4 + head_dim × bits / 8) — K blocks then V blocks, each block the codec's f32 norm followed by packed indices
representation.fixed_capacity_declared: per layer, the list of row allocations (Vec<Vec<u8>>): on a sliding layer its length never exceeds w + 1, so its capacity stops growing after warm-up (as window/v1's)

scratch.decision: one pair of f32 buffers (K, V) owned by the provider and reused across layers; prepare_layer(layer) resizes them to (end − base) × kv_dim and decodes every retained position's blocks into place; rows(layer) lends them through KvView::contiguous(base, kv_dim, ..) only when they hold THAT layer at its current end, and otherwise lends an empty view, which the step refuses by name
scratch.bound: capacity ≤ 2 × max_layer(end − base) × kv_dim × 4 bytes, as frozen; it only grows
scratch.codec_change: TurboQuant gains decode_block_into(&self, encoded, out: &mut [f32], scratch_u8) and decode_vector_into becomes a call to it — one decode path, writing into the scratch slice directly

C2.config: exactly `bits` ∈ {3, 4}; validate_config refuses a missing bits, any other value, and any other key, by name — no default

correction_before_merge.found_by: the C3 instrument's exact residency equation, on fixtures, before any model arm ran (developed stacked on this branch)

defects.packed_size: pack_3bit writes 3 bytes per group of up to 8 indices but packed_size(n, 3) declared ⌈3n/8⌉; for a head_dim not a multiple of 8 each 3-bit row outgrew its exact capacity and blocks were read back at a stride shorter than written (misaligned decode). V2's CompressedLayer strides by the same size. packed_size is now 3·⌈n/8⌉ — unchanged for every multiple of 8, so head_dims 64/128/256 were never affected
defects.codebook_static: the codec's Lloyd-Max table is a process-wide static built lazily on first encode — inside the first append, where it counted as append-born storage; now built at construction
defects.workspace_and_scratch: the encode workspace was first allocated inside append (now sized at announcement), and the scratch grew by amortised doubling, able to overshoot the frozen scratch bound (now exact growth)
